exec: Japan's police now have a dedicated team that can go to a cyberattack victim and preserve evidence; relevant to firms operating in Japan.
plain: Japan's National Police Agency started a team that goes to cyberattack victims, works with prefectural police and collects and preserves access logs, and advises on limiting damage and restoring systems.

sources.name: KAB 熊本朝日放送 (ANN): 相次ぐサイバー攻撃に対処 警察の専門部隊「FFF」発足

summary: According to ビジネス+IT, Japan's National Police Agency established the Fast Forensic Force (FFF), an initial-response forensics unit for cyberattacks, on 20 November. It is to go to the scene at a victim's or prefectural police force's request, preserve communication logs that give clues to unauthorized access, and advise on limiting damage; the article gives 153 personnel in total. KAB (ANN) also reports the 20 November launch, quoting Commissioner-General Kusu Yoshinobu.
title: Japan's National Police Agency launches Fast Forensic Force for cyberattack response

validation.note: Two independent publishers state the launch on 20 November: ビジネス+IT (sbbit.jp) and KAB 熊本朝日放送 (ANN network), which quotes NPA Commissioner-General Kusu Yoshinobu. The 153-personnel figure is from ビジネス+IT only. NPA's own release not read.

review.note: Compared 20 Nov launch, 153 personnel, dispatch, log preservation and advice with sbbit and KAB (Kusu quote)
